newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ICI, Unilever rise.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ICI, Unilever rise.

text.p: Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc (ICI) and Unilever Plc rose in New York Wednesday on news that Unilever would sell some units to ICI in an $8 billion deal.
Traders said American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were largely following Wall Street's lead in quiet trade.
"There aren't any standouts," a trader said. "There's Unilever and ICI, and they've got not necessarily fantastic volume."
ICI rose 3-1/8 to 50-3/8 and Unilever, an Anglo-Dutch chemical and consumer products group, was up 1-1/2 to 199. Volume in ICI was 360,000 shares in late morning, almost twice normal daily activity.
Unilever said it would sell its international specialty chemicals businesses to ICI for $8 billion in cash. ICI said the deal would remove its exposure to cyclical downturns in heavy chemicals.
Following the announcement, Merrill Lynch raised its near-term rating for ICI to accumulate from neutral.
Canadian software company Discreet Logic Inc rose 2-1/4 to 12-7/8 on volume that put it on the Nasdaq's most-active list.
The company late Tuesday reported record revenues and a profit for the third quarter against a loss for the same period in 1996.
Among Latin American shares, Telecom Argentina SA fell one to 50-1/8 after it reported second quarter earnings per share of $0.72, largely in line with analysts' expectations.
Traders attributed the drop to profit-taking. Morgan Stanley kept its outperform rating and J.P. Morgan its buy recommendation on the stock.
Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA fell 3/8 to 118-1/8.
Decliners led advancers 229 to 208 among 806 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.08 percent in late morning and volume was 47 million ADRs.
